sehemu: Part III: The Prime Minister, the Cabinet and the Government
jina: Attorney-General of the Government of the United Republic
maudhui: (1) There shall be an Attorney-General of the Government of the United Republic who shall be appointed by the President. (2) The Attorney-General shall be appointed from among public officers qualified to practise as advocates, or persons qualified to be registered as advocates, who have continuously held such qualifications for a period of not less than fifteen years. (3) The Attorney-General shall be the adviser to the Government of the United Republic on matters of law and, for that purpose, shall be responsible for advising the Government on all legal matters and for performing any other functions of a legal nature or connected with law. (4) In the discharge of his functions under this Article, the Attorney-General shall have the right to appear and be heard in all courts in the United Republic. (5) The Attorney-General shall be a Member of Parliament by virtue of his office and shall hold office until - (a) his appointment is revoked by the President; or (b) immediately before the President-elect assumes the office of President; and shall be paid a salary, allowances and other remuneration in accordance with a law enacted by Parliament.
vifungu: (1) There shall be an Attorney-General of the Government of the United Republic who shall be appointed by the President.

(2) The Attorney-General shall be appointed from among public officers qualified to practise as advocates, or persons qualified to be registered as advocates, who have continuously held such qualifications for a period of not less than fifteen years.

(3) The Attorney-General shall be the adviser to the Government of the United Republic on matters of law and, for that purpose, shall be responsible for advising the Government on all legal matters and for performing any other functions of a legal nature or connected with law.
(4) In the discharge of his functions under this Article, the Attorney-General shall have the right to appear and be heard in all courts in the United Republic.

(5) The Attorney-General shall be a Member of Parliament by virtue of his office and shall hold office until - (a) his appointment is revoked by the President; or (b) immediately before the President-elect assumes the office of President; and shall be paid a salary, allowances and other remuneration in accordance with a law enacted by Parliament.
